About Syngene

Incorporated in 1993, Syngene International Ltd. is an innovation-focused global discovery, development and manufacturing organization providing integrated scientific services to the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, nutrition, animal health, consumer goods and specialty chemical industries around the world. Syngene’ s clientele includes world leaders such as Bristol-Myers Squibb, Baxter, Amgen, GSK, Merck KGaA and Herbalife. Its innovative culture is driven by the passion of its 4240- strong team of scientists who work with clients from around the world to solve their scientific problems, improve R&D productivity, speed up time to market and lower the cost of innovation.

At Syngene, safety is at the heart of everything we do personally and professionally. Syngene has placed safety at par with business performance with shared responsibility and accountability, including following safety guidelines, procedures and SOPs, in letter and spirit.

The Director, Engineering and Maintenance provides strategic and technical leadership across engineering, facilities, and maintenance functions. The Director partners with senior leadership to drive capital projects, continuous improvement, and technology implementation to enhance equipment reliability, site capabilities, and operational performance. The director is accountable for Facilities operations, ensuring maintenance, utilities, and infrastructure are effectively maintained. Additionally, this role establishes engineering standards, supports new product introductions, and builds and develops high-performing team.

Oversee Facilities, Utilities, Maintenance, and Engineering functions, ensuring alignment with site and business objectives
Oversight of capital project planning and execution, including scope development, budgeting, scheduling, and implementation
Ensure facilities, utilities, and equipment are maintained in accordance with industry best practices and regulatory requirements
Accountable for all Quality Systems within the Engineering and Maintenance functions, including Deviations, CAPAs, SOP revisions (routine and biennial), and Change Control
Provide guidance, leadership and directives to support and comply with all health and safety policies and procedures
Develop and execute departmental goals, strategies, and long-term plans aligned with organizational objectives
Provide end-to-end technical leadership across design, implementation, and lifecycle management of equipment and systems
Provide oversight and support for technology transfers, equipment upgrades, and facility expansions
Establish and maintain engineering standards, best practices, and governance across all systems and processes
Lead cross-functional teams to drive equipment reliability, operational efficiency, and continuous improvement initiatives
Serve as a departmental point of contact during internal and external audits and regulatory inspections
Collaborate with senior leadership to develop business cases, resource plans, and engineering strategies
Manage departmental budgets, resource allocation, and site capital planning.
Oversee external engineering contractors, consultants, and service providers
Support troubleshooting and resolution of complex technical issues impacting manufacturing and facility systems and operations
Promote professional development of staff through coaching, mentoring, and training

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Chemical, Industrial, or related field) required
Experienced in a biopharmaceutical or biotechnology environment, with leadership experience in engineering and/or facilities management
Demonstrated career progression with increasing scope of responsibility, leadership, and organizational impact
Extensive knowledge of cGMP requirements, regulatory expectations, and compliance in a highly regulated environment
Ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams and align engineering strategy with business objectives
Experience in facility planning, asset lifecycle management, and infrastructure strategy
Technical expertise in facility systems, utilities, and manufacturing equipment within cGMP environments
Working knowledge of Quality Systems, including deviations, investigations, CAPAs, and change control processes
Experience managing budgets, capital planning, and cost optimization

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all organizational levels

The Role

The Sr. Director of Software Development leads our engineering organization with a sharp focus on quality, platform stability, and execution discipline across a complex, mature software ecosystem. This role ensures that software delivered to franchisees and customers is reliable, predictable, and scalable, and that issues are prevented early in the development lifecycle rather than discovered late or in production.

This role pairs executive leadership with strong technical depth. The Sr. Director of Software Development will establish development standards, enforce accountability, and partner cross-functionally to streamline release processes while remaining close enough to the architecture to review complex implementations and drive root-cause problem solving.

Work Location: This position follows a hybrid work schedule. We are seeking candidates based in the Greater Los Angeles area, or within a reasonable commuting distance, who can work from our Los Angeles headquarters on Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday to support collaboration and business needs. Remote work is available on the remaining weekdays.

Work Authorization: Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer sponsorship. At this time, we are unable to sponsor or transfer employment visas. Candidates who require visa sponsorship now or in the future will not be considered.

Engineering Leadership & Process Discipline

Establish and enforce a strong Definition of Done (DoD) so work is complete, thoroughly tested, and production-ready before deployment.
Drive execution discipline and accountability across Software Development for correctness, completeness, and system impact.
Streamline release processes to improve predictability, reduce last-minute deployment risk, and eliminate post-release fixes.
Build a culture of engineering excellence through accountability, ownership, continuous improvement, and disciplined execution.

Platform Quality & Technical Execution

Own overall platform stability and output quality, systematically minimizing regressions and production defects.
Provide technical leadership and guidance, including reviewing complex architectural implementations and ensuring sound design decisions.
Ensure developers understand, design for, and manage cross-system dependencies in a complex multi-tenant environment.
Lead root-cause analysis (RCA) for production incidents and implement systemic safeguards to prevent recurrence.
Develop and execute technical improvement plans that address technical debt, simplify architecture, improve maintainability, and increase long-term platform reliability.
Own the quality of software releases by ensuring engineering practices, validation, and release readiness consistently reduce production defects and improve predictability.
Help establish and enforce Definition of Ready (DoR) and Definition of Done (DoD) standards to improve execution quality throughout the development lifecycle.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Talent Development

Partner closely with Product and QA leadership to ensure requirements are build-ready upstream before development begins.
Mentor and coach Senior Developers and Developers, fostering their technical growth while strengthening problem-solving abilities, technical expertise, and overall execution across the team.
Collaborate cross-functionally to align software delivery with broader business imperatives and franchisee operational needs.

The strongest candidate is part executive leader and part technical strategist: someone who has a track record of instilling discipline and reducing incidents in complex software systems, but who can still go deep into architectural and debugging discussions when needed.

Experience: Typically 10+ years of progressive software engineering experience, including at least 5 years leading software development organizations with responsibility for engineering quality, delivery, and people leadership.
Leadership Background: Proven experience leading software engineering organizations (VP, Director, or Head of Engineering level) within mid-sized, growing companies (approx. 100–1,000 employees).
Hands-on Technical Credibility: Earlier in their career, the successful candidate was an accomplished software engineer and still possesses the technical depth to challenge architectural decisions, mentor senior engineers, and quickly understand complex production issues.
System Experience: Significant experience working on mature, complex codebases and multi-tenant SaaS platforms.
Quality & SDLC Track Record: Demonstrated success improving software quality, stabilizing platforms, reducing production incidents, and enforcing SDLC discipline.
Systems Mindset: Thinks in terms of full system health rather than isolated features, with a relentless focus on preventing problems before they hit production.
Decisive & Accountable: Comfortable setting a high bar, enforcing development standards, holding teams accountable, and making tough technical decisions.
Cross-Functional Communicator: Strong communicator who effectively translates technical risks and system trade-offs for Product, QA, and executive leadership.

jobs.description:
Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands.

About The Role

The Senior Manager, Salesforce Platform Engineering leads a team of Salesforce engineers responsible for building and supporting reliable, secure, and scalable solutions across our Salesforce platform. This role owns the engineering behind our Go-To-Market processes, spanning Lead-to-Opportunity, Opportunity-to-Quote, and Quote-to-Cash, along with the integrations that connect Salesforce to billing, provisioning, ERP, and enterprise data warehouse systems, while managing, mentoring, and growing the engineers who deliver them. The ideal candidate combines hands-on Salesforce platform development and data migration/integration experience with proven team leadership, and is fluent in applying cutting-edge AI technologies to real engineering work.

What You’ll Do

Own and lead engineering delivery for Salesforce-based Go-To-Market platforms supporting Lead-to-Opportunity, Opportunity-to-Quote, and Quote-to-Cash processes.
Lead and manage a team of engineers, including hiring, onboarding, workforce planning, regular feedback, performance management, and career development.
Drive platform modernization and consolidation efforts, including org consolidation, data migrations, and lifecycle improvements delivered with strong data integrity and minimal business disruption.
Partner with product, sales operations, revenue operations, business stakeholders, QA, data warehouse, and data quality teams to align priorities, manage risk, and deliver successful outcomes.
Champion the adoption of cutting-edge AI technologies within the team, applying AI-powered tools and agentic approaches beyond basic chat use, to automate workflows, accelerate delivery, and improve sales and service productivity.
Improve platform health by simplifying data flows, reducing technical debt, strengthening data quality controls, and improving observability and supportability.
Advance engineering practices through CI/CD automation, static code analysis, AI engineering, and code review standards.
Guide technical decisions through design reviews, code and automation reviews, troubleshooting, and knowledge sharing.

What You’ll Bring

7+ years of experience in software engineering, with 5+ years developing on the Salesforce platform.
4+ years of people management experience leading Salesforce or enterprise engineering teams, including hiring, performance management, and career development. Experience leading other leaders.
Hands-on experience developing on the Salesforce platform (Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flow, REST/SOAP APIs, and related tools), with strong expertise in Salesforce data modeling, SQL, SOQL, CPQ and Quote-to-Cash architectures, security, automation, platform design patterns, and data lifecycle management.
Proven experience designing, delivering, and supporting integrations, migrations, transformations, reconciliations, and monitoring across Salesforce and enterprise systems; direct hands-on experience with org consolidations, org-to-org data migrations, or Salesforce-to-Salesforce integrations strongly preferred.
Experience across Salesforce Sales, Revenue, and Experience Clouds, with a working understanding of GTM processes such as lead management, forecasting, territory management, renewals, and amendments. Experience with CPQ or Agentic Revenue Management strongly preferred.
Experience with CI/CD and DevOps tooling for Salesforce (such as Git, Jenkins, Gearset, Copado, or similar) and with enterprise ETL or data movement tools (such as MuleSoft, DB Amp or Apache HOP).
Demonstrated, hands-on proficiency with cutting-edge AI technologies, such as building or deploying AI agents, LLM-powered automation, or applied AI/ML tooling in engineering workflows, beyond general-purpose chat usage.
Strong strategic prioritization and problem-solving skills, including triage, debugging, performance optimization, root cause analysis, and incident support.
Clear communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence technical direction and align senior stakeholders across technical and non-technical teams.
Experience leading distributed, global, or vendor/offshore teams preferred.

Bonus Skills

Salesforce Administrator, Platform App Builder, or Salesforce Platform Developer certifications required.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent practical experience also considered.
Demonstrated application of AI/agentic tooling in professional projects (portfolio, case studies, or concrete examples) strongly preferred.

This role provides both administrative and technical leadership for engineering operations.

As a member of the Lilly Site Lead Team, the Senior Director contributes to shaping the site’s strategic direction, building organizational capability, and managing cross-functional issues. The team works collectively to achieve long-term business objectives, adapt to evolving corporate and external environments, and develop the site for future success.

Leadership Development: Cultivate future technical and managerial leaders for the site and potential global roles.

The Opportunity

Our client is building the infrastructure backbone of the AI era, developing large-scale, purpose-built data center campuses engineered for hyperscale computing. With committed capital, campuses in active development, and ambitious growth plans, the business requires a disciplined and sophisticated capital markets function.
Our client is seeking a Head of Investor Relations to lead relationships with the investors supporting its growth. As the business expands across multiple campuses and financing structures, its investor base will grow in size and complexity—spanning institutional equity, project finance, corporate debt, and potentially the public markets.
This executive will shape how the company communicates its strategy, reports its progress, and earns investors’ confidence. It is a company-defining opportunity to build the capital narrative and investor relations function of a rapidly growing infrastructure platform.

The Role

Reporting to the President and working closely with the CEO and CFO, the Head of Investor Relations will serve as the primary bridge between our client and its investors.
The successful candidate will own the investor narrative, reporting strategy, and relationships across the capital stack. They will translate operational progress into a clear and credible investment story for equity investors, lenders, and rating agencies while establishing the reporting systems and disclosure practices needed to support future fundraising and growth.

Key Responsibilities

Investor Narrative and Positioning

Own and continually refine the company’s equity story and investment thesis as its portfolio, financing structures, and market conditions evolve.
Develop messaging, presentations, supporting data, and other materials for each stage of capital formation.
Position the company within the competitive landscape of infrastructure, data center, and AI platforms.
Partner with the President, CEO, and CFO on board presentations, investor updates, and capital markets communications.

Capital Raising and Transaction Support

Support equity and debt raises from initial preparation through closing, including materials, data-room management, diligence coordination, and investor inquiries.
Build and maintain the diligence infrastructure required to act quickly when financing opportunities arise.
Coordinate with the CFO, outside counsel, and financial advisors during active transactions.
Maintain the fundraising pipeline and track relationships with existing and prospective investors.

Connect operational progress—including campuses under construction, megawatts contracted, and capital deployed—to the financial outcomes investors are underwriting.
Manage investor communications between formal reporting cycles and respond to inquiries regarding material developments.
Establish disclosure standards and information controls appropriate for future engagement with debt and public markets.

Relationship Management

Serve as the day-to-day relationship lead for institutional investors and private equity stakeholders.
Build relationships with prospective investors, lenders, and rating agencies ahead of future capital requirements.
Manage rating-agency engagement as the company approaches larger debt facilities.
Represent the company at investor meetings, roadshows, and industry conferences.

Market Intelligence

Monitor capital markets activity across the data center, AI, and broader infrastructure sectors.
Track comparable financings, valuation benchmarks, public-company performance, and investor sentiment.
Incorporate relevant market intelligence into capital planning and positioning decisions.

Investor Relations Function Development

Build the investor relations function, including the systems, processes, reporting infrastructure, and future team.
Establish scalable investor relationship management and disclosure controls.
Design information flows that keep leadership, the board, and investors aligned as the company grows.

At least 5 years of experience in investor relations, capital markets, private equity, investment banking, or infrastructure finance.
A proven track record supporting equity and debt raises in capital-intensive businesses.
Strong understanding of the metrics and reporting expected by institutional infrastructure investors.
Experience managing relationships with institutional investors, lenders, or rating agencies.
Strong financial acumen and familiarity with project finance structures, capital models, and board-level reporting.

Demonstrated ability to translate operational and financial information into a compelling investment narrative.
Experience working in a high-growth, institutionally backed, capital-intensive environment.

Candidates may have experience in one or more of the following areas:
Investor relations leadership within an infrastructure, energy, real estate, or data center business.
Investment or capital markets experience at a private equity firm, infrastructure fund, or investment bank, ideally with exposure to digital infrastructure.
A Head of Investor Relations, Vice President of Investor Relations, or senior capital markets role at a high-growth or publicly traded infrastructure company.
Supporting a significant capital raise, refinancing, or transition toward public-market readiness.
Working across the capital stack, from institutional equity and project finance to corporate debt.

Leadership Profile

The successful candidate will:
Operate with the discipline, accuracy, and judgment required to establish capital markets credibility.
Communicate complex financial and operational information clearly to sophisticated audiences.
Build trusted relationships with investors, executives, board members, and colleagues.
Be comfortable creating systems and processes where little infrastructure currently exists.
Communicate credibly with both internal finance teams and external stakeholders.
Thrive in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment with high standards and significant growth ambitions.

60–100% of base salary, performance-linked

Head of Investor Relations
US-Based | Executive Leadership

The Opportunity

Our client is building the infrastructure backbone of the AI era, developing large-scale, purpose-built data center campuses engineered for hyperscale computing. With committed capital, campuses in active development, and ambitious growth plans, the business requires a disciplined and sophisticated capital markets function.
Our client is seeking a Head of Investor Relations to lead relationships with the investors supporting its growth. As the business expands across multiple campuses and financing structures, its investor base will grow in size and complexity—spanning institutional equity, project finance, corporate debt, and potentially the public markets.
This executive will shape how the company communicates its strategy, reports its progress, and earns investors’ confidence. It is a company-defining opportunity to build the capital narrative and investor relations function of a rapidly growing infrastructure platform.

The Role

Reporting to the President and working closely with the CEO and CFO, the Head of Investor Relations will serve as the primary bridge between our client and its investors.
The successful candidate will own the investor narrative, reporting strategy, and relationships across the capital stack. They will translate operational progress into a clear and credible investment story for equity investors, lenders, and rating agencies while establishing the reporting systems and disclosure practices needed to support future fundraising and growth.

Key Responsibilities

Investor Narrative and Positioning

Own and continually refine the company’s equity story and investment thesis as its portfolio, financing structures, and market conditions evolve.
Develop messaging, presentations, supporting data, and other materials for each stage of capital formation.
Position the company within the competitive landscape of infrastructure, data center, and AI platforms.
Partner with the President, CEO, and CFO on board presentations, investor updates, and capital markets communications.

Capital Raising and Transaction Support

Support equity and debt raises from initial preparation through closing, including materials, data-room management, diligence coordination, and investor inquiries.
Build and maintain the diligence infrastructure required to act quickly when financing opportunities arise.
Coordinate with the CFO, outside counsel, and financial advisors during active transactions.
Maintain the fundraising pipeline and track relationships with existing and prospective investors.

Investor Reporting and Communications

Own the cadence and quality of investor reporting, including quarterly updates, capital-deployment reporting, and key infrastructure metrics.
Connect operational progress—including campuses under construction, megawatts contracted, and capital deployed—to the financial outcomes investors are underwriting.
Manage investor communications between formal reporting cycles and respond to inquiries regarding material developments.
Establish disclosure standards and information controls appropriate for future engagement with debt and public markets.

Relationship Management

Serve as the day-to-day relationship lead for institutional investors and private equity stakeholders.
Build relationships with prospective investors, lenders, and rating agencies ahead of future capital requirements.
Manage rating-agency engagement as the company approaches larger debt facilities.
Represent the company at investor meetings, roadshows, and industry conferences.

Market Intelligence

Monitor capital markets activity across the data center, AI, and broader infrastructure sectors.
Track comparable financings, valuation benchmarks, public-company performance, and investor sentiment.
Incorporate relevant market intelligence into capital planning and positioning decisions.

Investor Relations Function Development

Build the investor relations function, including the systems, processes, reporting infrastructure, and future team.
Establish scalable investor relationship management and disclosure controls.
Design information flows that keep leadership, the board, and investors aligned as the company grows.

Qualifications

Required Experience

At least 5 years of experience in investor relations, capital markets, private equity, investment banking, or infrastructure finance.
A proven track record supporting equity and debt raises in capital-intensive businesses.
Strong understanding of the metrics and reporting expected by institutional infrastructure investors.
Experience managing relationships with institutional investors, lenders, or rating agencies.
Strong financial acumen and familiarity with project finance structures, capital models, and board-level reporting.
Experience creating investor materials and managing diligence during active transactions.
Demonstrated ability to translate operational and financial information into a compelling investment narrative.
Experience working in a high-growth, institutionally backed, capital-intensive environment.

Preferred Background

Candidates may have experience in one or more of the following areas:
Investor relations leadership within an infrastructure, energy, real estate, or data center business.
Investment or capital markets experience at a private equity firm, infrastructure fund, or investment bank, ideally with exposure to digital infrastructure.
A Head of Investor Relations, Vice President of Investor Relations, or senior capital markets role at a high-growth or publicly traded infrastructure company.
Supporting a significant capital raise, refinancing, or transition toward public-market readiness.
Working across the capital stack, from institutional equity and project finance to corporate debt.

Leadership Profile

The successful candidate will:
Operate with the discipline, accuracy, and judgment required to establish capital markets credibility.
Communicate complex financial and operational information clearly to sophisticated audiences.
Build trusted relationships with investors, executives, board members, and colleagues.
Be comfortable creating systems and processes where little infrastructure currently exists.
Communicate credibly with both internal finance teams and external stakeholders.
Thrive in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment with high standards and significant growth ambitions.

Compensation and Benefits

Our client offers a highly competitive executive compensation package, with meaningful equity participation designed to align the successful candidate with long-term company performance.
Base salary:
$250,000–$325,000
Annual cash bonus:
60–100% of base salary, performance-linked
Equity:
Significant equity participation reflecting build-phase risk and potential upside
Equity vesting:
Three- to four-year schedule
Benefits:
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

Actual compensation will depend on experience, qualifications, location, and other relevant factors.

About Our Client

Our client develops and operates next-generation data center campuses designed to support AI, cloud, and enterprise computing at scale. Its platform combines deep infrastructure expertise, institutional capital, and the belief that physical infrastructure will be one of the defining constraints—and opportunities—of the next phase of AI adoption.

The organization moves quickly, maintains high standards, and gives accomplished operators the opportunity to shape both the business and its long-term success.

To express interest or make a confidential referral, please contact the partner leading the search - Tom Perkin.
